about: Every observable capability of the skill, one id each, with the criteria (criteria.jsonl ids) that judge it. Bundled briefs claim the features they exercise in their brief.json; coverage.py fails unless every feature is claimed by a brief whose profile selects one of its criteria in a concern the brief scopes. spec = the development spec that built it. A new capability adds its feature here, a criterion that judges it and a brief that exercises it.

features.description: One self-contained HTML file that opens offline and trips no endpoint heuristics
Slides authored only with the documented data attributes and component classes, no per-slide styling or scripts
One shared SVG defs block (lift shadows, arrowheads) referenced by every diagram and coloured by the palette
One input = one step forward or back by keys, click and wheel; Home/End; slides left only after their last step
data-show-at / data-hide-at / data-at reveal, swap and step-only elements; step-list current/done states
Title bar with chapter agenda built from data-chapter, compact mode when crowded, and a progress hairline
Step-only overlays shown at exactly one step, softening the slide beneath and handing over to a successor
Reader notes mode: spotlight veil and ring, numbered pins, callout with cited sources, prev/next/close bar
Seeded ambient orb layer behind data-ambient slides, drifting only while the slide is current
Diagram tiles get centred text and shared baselines; data-from/data-to edges are drawn gapped between tile rects
prefers-reduced-motion and notes mode land every transition at its end; no travel, scale or blur motion
window.deck (ready, state, goto, next, prev, plan) for tools and tests, and the module hook API
Persistent scene diagram across slides with a camera, parts arriving by scene point, soft/backdrop/dim/muted states
Narration column of message tiles placed by the module, one per step, with rack-focus exits
Up to two opaque, shadowed pop-over tiles with illustrations over the softened scene
Row of two to four equal frosted text tiles, one per step, tightening on short screens
Lead title slide: big title, body below, vertically centred, byline pinned bottom-left
Closing slide: one lead-size line centred on the page, no kicker
Standard kicker / title / body grid below the bar with a centred flow body
Split body (36/64, or flipped 64/36) placing text or a step list beside a diagram
Stacked body: a full-width diagram taking the free height with a quote or caption under it
Layered body whose build phases share one cell and swap by step
Figure column: a diagram with short annotation cards under it that swap by step
Three-column scene layout: body, scene slot and narration, title spanning the top
Timeline body: dated entries appearing one per step with sub-entries, none shown ahead
Kicker, title (at most one italic phrase, balanced wrap) and byline slots
Body paragraphs, captions, a single-number stat with its label, and quotations with a cite line
Dash-bulleted points at text size
Numbered step list with waiting, current and done discs and sub-entries
Term/definition columns, each topped by a soft rule
Numbered discussion prompts on accent discs
Tables with a kicker-style header, soft row rules and an emphasised first column
Staggered slide entry and the rise of revealed parts, per the style's motion tokens
Insight overlay: one frosted card with a serif statement, rack-focus exit, body softened beneath
In-flow message card: sender, verbatim quote and cite
Diagram tiles with title and sub text, scaled so text never drops below its type floor
Key tile: the accent-tinted, glowing tile that marks a diagram's focus
Gapped edges with matching heads: default, reinforced, ok and loss
Tracked-caps labels and tags (loss variant) placed beside what they name
Domain regions naming where things run, with an outside variant
Line-drawn actors: dots (ink, loss, alarm), singled-out rings and hairline links (lit, bold, ink)
Status badges on tile corners: tick, key, padlock; loss and off variants
Document and folder glyphs and quiet line icons
Lifted annotation cards with a coloured run-in label, never a side bar
Source links underlined in the surrounding text colour, never blue
Notes toggle, veil, spotlight ring, pins, callout and notes bar styling
One-row legend under a scene diagram whose entries may arrive by scene point
Small line-drawn pop-over illustrations: frames, boxes, actors, tries that draw and fail, flags, docs
Default palette: paper, charcoal and one decorative green accent that is never text
Second palette: four bright primaries on white as fills and strokes, darker ink roles for accent text
Editorial style: serif/sans pairing, type scale, bokeh, frost, shadows and motion curves
WCAG contrast gate over each palette's declared pairs, never rounded up, blocking output on failure
DTCG token files generate the CSS theme blocks and the PPTX colour and font schemes
Each style effect declares native, approximated or lost for PowerPoint
Build a new deck from the skeleton with the chosen palette and style and embedded fonts
Swap an existing deck's theme blocks only, leaving slides byte-identical
List endpoint-safety faults in a deck
Screenshot every slide x step x review size (and reader notes) of any deck
Check every slide x step x size for overlap, overflow, off-canvas and occlusion
Measure each slide's final state and per-step deltas in Chrome into a scene file
Emit an editable PPTX: master layouts with placeholders, theme slots, named native shapes, speaker notes
Build steps as native entrance, exit, emphasis and motion-path animations, Morph only where none fits
Validate the package and timing and write PX verdicts in the eval schema
Re-flow an emitted PPTX into a foreign corporate template's layouts and theme
Storyboard method: message codes, chapters, timings, per-slide visual, overlays, sources, approval marks
Every claim cited to a quality-tagged source with page or section, via an index and strand notes
Single-sourced, disputed, paraphrased and thin claims flagged on the slide or in its note
Verbatim quotes checked against the source, cuts marked, paraphrase never shown as a quote
Copy written to the presenter's voice profile: rules plus approved and rejected pairs
Install the project AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and PRD/SPEC/ADR templates into a fresh deck project
Merge the process into an existing AGENTS.md without overwriting it, keeping the project's wording
Intent lands in the PRD before the spec and the code on every change
Interview the presenter one question at a time, never multi-option pickers
Ask before researching and record the consent
Prototype new visual language and judge it by eye, or record the presenter's in-situ choice
Spec, failing tests committed red, build to green, done claims borne out by diffs and tests
Layout guard on and assembled screenshots at every affected step and size looked at before done
Worked example: cited excerpts per part, the rejected first draft and the assembled HF subset decks
Criterion library defined once: concern, evidence type, binary or fully described scale, anchors, flaws
Deck-type profiles select and weight criteria, declare gates and own profile-only criteria
Scope prompt, evidence capture, isolated generic judge subagents, k repeats and dated run folders
Deterministic gate runner checking every D criterion on a deck and its repo, in the judge verdict format
Judge prompt templates for output and process: evidence, rationale, score or insufficient evidence
Validate verdicts, take medians, flag spread, fail on gates and write the report with calibration status
Pairwise skill-version A/B judged in both orders, disagreement as a tie
Deliberately flawed anchor decks and a clean control, labelled with the criteria they must fail or pass
Bundled test briefs with fixed research packs, built and judged the same way every run
Replace or extract an existing deck's SLIDES block (the slides' source of truth), re-deriving module blocks
Per-step text extracts from the rendered deck (titles, blocks, notes, sources) for text judges
Labelled contact sheets of every slide x step so deck-scope judges see every state
Anchor judge-accuracy table: labelled must_fail/must_pass against aggregated verdicts
Several targets in one run as sub-runs under a suite manifest, with a roll-up report
Closing slide that sets the finding at title size over centred discussion prompts
Chart parts in the diagram kit: bars, square swatches, axis, gridline, dashed target, start/end labels
